detail.longDescription: Adding yourself to the docker group is root on the host, and Docker's post-install page says so in a warning box: "The docker group grants root-level privileges to the user." One bind mount of / into a container reaches the whole host filesystem, with no sudo prompt and nothing in the sudo log. Rootless mode removes the root daemon, and plain sudo docker keeps every call logged. https:// techfuelhq.com/tutorials/add-u ser-to-docker-group-2026/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=distribution-2026-10&utm_content=docker-group-root-mastodon # selfhosted # Docker
